lines.text: Here is a model with seven billion weights, sitting in fourteen gigabytes of memory.
Now make it write a long document. Every token it writes gets stored.
Not just the token. The key and the value vector, for every layer, for every head.
That is the key-value cache. It is the reason long context is expensive.
The arithmetic for one token: thirty-two layers, each keeping a key and a value for every head.
That is about half a megabyte per token, in half precision, for a model this size.
A hundred thousand tokens of context is fifty gigabytes. For one conversation.
The model itself is fourteen gigabytes. The cache is now the bigger number.
Which flips the question. It is not how big is the model. It is how much are you going to ask it.
You can shrink the cache. Compress it, evict it, quantise it, or share the heads.
Every one of those is a trade. Compression costs accuracy, eviction costs context.
And none of them is free. They are all the same move: fit more context into less memory.
The model is the thing you trained. The cache is the thing you pay for.
